Israel, Lebanon hold US-mediated military talks as tensions mount over Hezbollah disarmament
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
05:16:22 UTC
14:16:22 KST

Military representatives from Israel, Lebanon and the United States began three days of talks Tuesday in Tampa, Florida, amid deep disagreements over Hezbollah's disarmament, continued Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon and growing uncertainty over the region's security arrangements.
The meetings, held at U.S. Central Command headquarters and scheduled to continue through Thursday, are strictly military in nature and do not constitute another round of direct political negotiations between Israel and Lebanon.
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun said Saturday that a military delegation would attend the meetings to present Beirut's demands for an end to Israeli military escalation.
"A Lebanese military delegation will participate to present Lebanon's demands for an end to Israeli escalation, in the hope of achieving results consistent with the framework agreement," Aoun said.
The talks come as diplomatic efforts between the two countries remain largely stalled, with Israel accusing the Lebanese Armed Forces of failing to dismantle Hezbollah's military infrastructure in designated areas of southern Lebanon. Lebanese officials, meanwhile, accuse Israel of repeatedly violating existing agreements and undermining efforts to stabilize the border.
Low expectations in Beirut
Lebanese officials have expressed little optimism about the prospect of a breakthrough in Tampa.
A Lebanese report published Tuesday quoted official sources as saying there were no signs of optimism surrounding the meetings.
"The United States, as is well known, imposed this round, and it is nothing more than an attempt to say that the negotiation process is still ongoing, even if it has produced no results," a senior official was quoted as saying.
The official described the timing as particularly unfavorable, with Israeli elections just a week away.
"This round comes at a dead time, considering that the elections in Israel are only a week away," the official said. "There is no reason to believe that Israel, which has offered Lebanon nothing since the framework agreement was signed, will offer anything this week or at any later point regarding a ceasefire or expanding the scope of the pilot zones."
The official accused Israel's political and security establishments of remaining committed to military operations in Lebanon and maintaining a presence south of the Litani River.
"The central principle upheld by Israel, both its political and security establishments, is the continuation of aggression against Lebanon and the refusal to withdraw from the area south of the Litani River," the official said. "They state this clearly."
Similar assessments emerged earlier this month.
On Oct. 13, the Saudi-owned Al Hadath television channel cited a Lebanese source as saying expectations for the Tampa meeting were limited.
The source claimed Israel was not cooperating with a U.S.-backed verification mechanism and instead wanted a direct operations room with the Lebanese military to verify conditions in the designated pilot zones, even after Lebanese troops had deployed there.
"Washington understands Beirut's concerns regarding Israel's demands," the source said.
At the center of the dispute are two pilot zones established in southern Lebanon as part of efforts to assess the Lebanese military's ability to remove Hezbollah weapons and infrastructure.
Israeli officials maintain that the Lebanese army has failed to clear the areas effectively, while Lebanon disputes Israel's account of its military operations and the implementation of existing agreements.
Despite the deadlock, U.S. officials have sought to maintain military-level engagement between the sides to prevent the diplomatic process from collapsing entirely.
Israeli operations draw criticism across Lebanon's political divide
The talks are taking place against the backdrop of continued Israeli military operations against Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.
The operations have drawn criticism from across Lebanon's political spectrum, including Hezbollah supporters and activists who have demanded a change in government policy, an end to direct negotiations with Israel and a complete Israeli withdrawal.
Criticism has also come from senior Lebanese officials opposed to Hezbollah's independent military activities, including Aoun and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam.
Both leaders have condemned Israeli strikes while maintaining their support for diplomacy as the preferred means of resolving the conflict.
"Israel has not complied with the framework agreement, and the southern region continues to be subjected to daily violations," Aoun said this week.
"These actions will not produce a positive outcome. They will only strengthen the Lebanese people's attachment to their land and their rights."
Aoun said continued Israeli operations were also obstructing the Lebanese government's efforts to achieve its security objectives.
"Lebanon remains committed to a diplomatic solution despite the difficulties," he said. "It comes at a much lower cost than a devastating war, whose price is paid by the Lebanese people, particularly the residents of the south. It is time for Lebanon to have some respite."
Fears grow over security vacuum after UN peacekeepers leave
The diplomatic uncertainty has been compounded by concerns about the future of the United Nations peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon, known as UNIFIL, whose mandate is scheduled to end later this year.
Lebanese authorities fear the mission's departure could create a security vacuum along the Israeli border and have called on the UN Security Council to establish an alternative arrangement.
UNIFIL said Tuesday that its personnel were continuing operations in Lebanon while the Security Council examined possible arrangements for the period following the mission's conclusion.
The issue has become a central concern in discussions between Lebanese officials and visiting foreign delegations.
The Saudi newspaper Asharq Al-Awsat quoted ministerial sources as saying regional tensions and the possibility of further deterioration had dominated recent meetings with international representatives visiting Lebanon.
According to the sources, the delegations warned Lebanese officials against becoming involved in another military confrontation.
"Lebanon received advice from the visiting delegations, which warned against being drawn into a new adventure," the sources said.
The warnings also suggested that a renewed confrontation could unfold under different conditions from previous rounds of fighting.
"The messages conveyed emphasize that in the event of a new confrontation, Israel will not be bound by the restrictions agreed upon in the past," the sources said.
IDF accuses Lebanese army of failing to act against Hezbollah
The dispute intensified Tuesday after the IDF publicly accused the Lebanese Armed Forces of failing to fulfill their responsibilities under security understandings reached in 2024.
In a statement issued by IDF Arabic-language spokesperson Lt. Col. Ella Waweya, the military said the Lebanese army had been tasked with preventing Hezbollah from maintaining weapons and military infrastructure in southern Lebanon.
"Under the 2024 understandings, which guided Israeli and Lebanese actions until Operation Roaring Lion, the Lebanese Army was responsible for acting against the presence of weapons and military infrastructure belonging to the Hezbollah terrorist organization in southern Lebanon," Waweya said, referring to the latest round of fighting between Israel and the Iran-backed terrorist group.
"However, this responsibility was not fulfilled as required, allowing Hezbollah to continue entrenching itself, arming itself, and building military infrastructure in the area."
The IDF said there remained a substantial gap between Lebanese declarations and conditions on the ground.
"Even during the Lebanese Army’s 2025 Operation Homeland Shield, a significant gap remained between statements and the reality on the ground, and the operation did not dismantle the terrorist organization’s military capabilities or prevent it from continuing its activities and buildup," Waweya said.
The IDF cited an incident involving a military facility in the southern Lebanese village of Kafra, which it said Hezbollah had used to store weapons.
According to the military, the facility was referred to the Lebanese army through the U.S.-led monitoring mechanism in December 2025.
The Lebanese army subsequently reported that it had addressed the site, the IDF said.
However, Israeli surveillance allegedly revealed several months later that Hezbollah continued operating at the facility and had removed weapons and military equipment to preserve its capabilities.
"Several months after the Lebanese Army had already declared that it had addressed the asset, Hezbollah was still able to use it for its own purposes," the military said.
The statement was accompanied by footage that the IDF said showed Hezbollah operatives loading weapons from the facility onto a truck.
The military said its forces struck and destroyed the truck after identifying the activity.
It also alleged that individuals within the Lebanese army had coordinated enforcement operations with Hezbollah, allowing the group advance warning to remove weapons and equipment.
"The Intelligence Directorate has identified instances in which elements within the Lebanese Army coordinated with Hezbollah regarding enforcement activities. This coordination assisted efforts to prevent, delay, or thwart enforcement operations and enabled Hezbollah to prepare in advance to remove and transfer weapons from the area," the statement said.
The IDF called on the Lebanese army to take more effective action against Hezbollah.
"The Lebanese Army is responsible for ensuring the full and thorough implementation of all tasks assigned to it," the military said.
"The IDF emphasizes that it expects the Lebanese Army to act more decisively and effectively to fulfill its responsibilities and prevent the presence of weapons and military infrastructure belonging to the Hezbollah terrorist organization in southern Lebanon."
The military added that Israeli forces and military intelligence would continue monitoring Hezbollah's attempts to rebuild its capabilities.
"The IDF and the Intelligence Directorate, continue to monitor Hezbollah’s attempts to rebuild and strengthen its capabilities and will not allow any violation that poses a threat to the State of Israel and its civilians," the statement said.
Lebanese army rejects allegations as false
The Lebanese Armed Forces rejected the Israeli accusations in an official statement Tuesday evening, calling them false and accusing Israel of attempting to undermine the army's credibility at home and abroad.
The Lebanese military presented a different account of the Kafra facility, saying its personnel began operating at the site in December 2025 and continued their work until March 16.
According to the statement, operations were suspended and the area evacuated following a request from the ceasefire monitoring mechanism after Israel threatened to strike the facility.
The Lebanese army said it had explicitly reported at the time that its mission remained incomplete and that military equipment and ammunition were still present.
"The army command clarifies that in December 2025, military units began operating at a military facility in the town of Kafra, in the Bint Jbeil district, and continued their activities until March 16," the statement said.
"Work at the facility was halted and the area evacuated at the request of the ceasefire monitoring mechanism, following Israeli threats to attack the site. The Lebanese army reported at the time that the mission had not been completed and that military equipment and ammunition remained there."
The army said it repeatedly requested permission to resume operations and remove the remaining equipment but was refused by Israel.
It said its units eventually resumed the mission on Aug. 16 in coordination with the ceasefire monitoring mechanism and completed the operation on Oct. 16, 2026, when the facility was closed.
The Lebanese military also challenged the authenticity of the IDF's account of the accompanying footage.
According to the Lebanese statement, the video showing a truck being struck by Israeli forces was recorded on July 3, 2026, in the Tyre area, about a week after the framework agreement was signed.
The army said the incident was unrelated to Israel's account of its handling of the Kafra facility.
"All events and activities are documented with the committee overseeing the ceasefire," the Lebanese military said. "This fact refutes the Israeli allegations."
The statement accused Israel of deliberately spreading misinformation during the ongoing negotiations.
"The false information and dissemination of lies by Israel are part of an attempt to undermine the Lebanese army's credibility domestically and internationally, in parallel with the negotiations taking place," it said.
"The army command reiterates its full commitment to fulfilling its duties and responsibilities, while Israel continues its attacks and violations of the existing understandings."
Netanyahu tells Lebanon to clear Hezbollah or Israel will act
Israel is represented at the Tampa meetings by two senior military officers: Maj. Gen. Tal Politis, the IDF's defense attaché in Washington, and Brig. Gen. Amichai Levin, head of the military's Strategic Division.
Although diplomatic contacts between Israel and Lebanon have largely stalled, U.S. officials considered the military meetings important for preserving momentum in the negotiations.
The central issue remains whether the Lebanese army can effectively dismantle Hezbollah's military infrastructure in the two designated pilot zones.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the dispute during a briefing when asked what Israel would demand at the meetings and whether it had set a deadline for the Lebanese army to disarm Hezbollah.
"We will demand one simple thing from them," Netanyahu said. "Please, the Lebanese army can go in. We gave you two test areas, 'pilot zones.' Go in and clear them. Can you do it? Good. Can't you? We'll take care of it."
Netanyahu said Israel would not allow threats from Hezbollah to accumulate along its northern border.
"We are not allowing these threats to build up," he said. "We are not operating only along the line. If they try to attack us, we go after them and strike. But you want to prove otherwise? By all means, prove it. Unfortunately, up to this moment, you haven't."
The prime minister nevertheless suggested there had been some limited changes in Lebanon's conduct.
"There is a certain change that we are seeing," he said, without elaborating.
Netanyahu also linked Hezbollah's elimination as a military force to the prospect of a broader diplomatic breakthrough with Lebanon.
"If Hezbollah is eliminated, as we will ensure happens, then certainly at that moment we will have a peace agreement with Lebanon, and very good things can happen," he said.
He further claimed that some Lebanese citizens, including Shiite Muslims, were hoping for his victory in the upcoming elections.
"There are Shiites who say, 'We want Netanyahu to win because it is essential for our future,'" he said.
Defense Minister Israel Katz reinforced the government's position, saying Israeli forces would remain in the security zone until Hezbollah was fully disarmed.
"The IDF will not move from the security zone as long as Hezbollah has not been disarmed throughout Lebanon and the threat to residents of northern Israel has not been removed," Katz said.

Rubio says US envoy to discuss Ukraine security proposals with Russia
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
05:13:57 UTC
14:13:57 KST

Diyar Guldogan
21 October 2026•Update: 21 October 2026
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that US envoy Steve Witkoff was expected to present ideas on Ukraine’s long-term security to Russian officials following a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Speaking to reporters in India, Rubio said Witkoff had met Zelenskyy on Tuesday in Norway and was traveling to St. Petersburg, Russia, to discuss the proposals with the Russian side.
"I believe he just left Norway, but he met with Zelenskyy, and so I think they floated some ideas. He wanted to go there first. He's on his way to St. Petersburg. My understanding, he might even be underway as we speak, and I think he'll share some ideas," Rubio said.
Rubio said Ukraine’s main priority was to secure guarantees that would prevent future Russian attacks.
“I think for Ukraine, the predominant desire is to ensure their long-term security and safety, so that they’re never re-invaded or re-attacked in the future,” he said.
The secretary described the meeting between Witkoff and Zelenskyy as "positive," saying the envoy would take the ideas discussed to Russia in an effort to advance negotiations.
"My understanding from the information he provided to me and the readout I got from it, is that it was positive, nothing unexpected, nothing surprising, and he'll now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St. Petersburg and share them with the Russian side, and let's see if we can make some progress."
Rubio also defended the Trump administration’s role in supporting Kyiv, arguing that US assistance had been critical to Ukraine’s survival as an independent state.
“If it were not for the assistance of the United States, including under the Trump administration, there would be no Ukraine right now,” he said. “Ukraine as a sovereign state would not exist.”
President Donald Trump said Tuesday that the EU is getting “tired of spending” money on Ukraine and urged Zelenskyy to reach a deal to end the war with Russia.
Asked whether the peace process was back on track after the talks in Oslo, he said: “I think what’s happening is that Russia would like to get it done.”
“Russia is a big machine. They just keep grinding forward,” he said. “They have an unlimited supply of people.”

More trouble for CJP leaders: Another FIR against Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka transferred to Crime Branch
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
05:12:52 UTC
14:12:52 KST

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police has transferred a second FIR registered against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to the Crime Branch, which will now investigate both cases linked to the activists' alleged entry into Connaught Place and Jantar Mantar, sources said on Wednesday.Two cases were registered on October 13 following protests by CJP members at the two locations without approval, according to news agency ANI.
The case related to Connaught Place was transferred to the Crime Branch on Tuesday, while the second case, concerning Jantar Mantar, has also now been handed over to the unit, sources said.According to news agency PTI, the police alleged that Das, Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and 11 other CJP members entered the Jantar Mantar area on October 13 by trespassing through private premises. Jantar Mantar has been denotified as a designated protest site.Police personnel deployed at the spot intervened, and all 14 people were detained. Two FIRs were subsequently registered.
CJP leaders move Delhi High Court against custody extension
Meanwhile, Das and Ranka have approached the Delhi High Court challenging an order extending their judicial custody, arguing that their continued detention despite furnishing sureties violates their fundamental right to personal liberty.
Their legal team has challenged the October 19 order passed by a Special Executive Magistrate in New Delhi district under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).According to their lawyers, the magistrate rejected fresh sureties submitted by the two leaders on October 19 and directed them to explain why there should not be an apprehension of a breach of peace.The legal team contends that the continued detention is arbitrary and contrary to established legal principles. The leaders have sought the setting aside of the order, arguing that their detention infringes their constitutional right to personal liberty under Article 21.The matter is scheduled to be taken up by the High Court on Wednesday.The leaders sought an urgent hearing on Tuesday, including a night hearing, as the High Court remains closed for the Dussehra vacation.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh said in a post on X, "We have moved the Delhi high court and requested an urgent night hearing. Saurav and Ashutosh should not spend a single minute behind bars. Their liberty must not be curtailed because of political games. Justice must not wait."The party has alleged that bail proceedings have been deliberately delayed to prevent the release of its two co-convenors, the newspaper reported.
According to their legal team, Das and Ranka were first detained on October 10 after arriving at Terminal 3 of the Indira Gandhi International Airport. Preventive proceedings were initiated against them the following day, after which they were released on executing bonds of Rs 50,000 each.They were detained again on October 13 after going to Jantar Mantar carrying the national flag. They were subsequently shown as arrested under Sections 126 and 170 of the BNSS on October 14.A Special Executive Magistrate sent the two leaders to five-day judicial custody on October 14 for allegedly breaching peace bonds. Their custody was extended by two days on Monday after police sought further detention, citing apprehensions of a breach of peace.

UN sees higher global warming, even in best-case scenario
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
05:06:23 UTC
14:06:23 KST

UN sees higher global warming, even in best-case scenario
- UN report says global warming may reach 1.7 deg C to 1.8 deg C higher by mid-century, even in the best case, and “urgent and stringent” cuts are still needed.
- Current policies point to 2.8 deg C warming by 2100, or 2.6 deg C if pledges are fully met, both higher than 2025 forecasts.
- Antonio Guterres said “Overshoot is not surrender”, but returning to 1.5 deg C may depend on large-scale carbon removal, which is still uncertain.
AI generated
LONDON – Global warming is now projected to exceed previous estimates, with even the most optimistic scenario seeing average temperatures rise to 1.7 deg C to 1.8 deg C above pre-industrial levels by mid-century, a UN report showed on Oct 21.
Despite a rapid expansion of renewable energy and climate policies that are reducing emissions in many countries, the report said “urgent and stringent” cuts were still needed to achieve that best-case outcome.
The UN Environment Programme’s report said greenhouse gas emissions would need to fall 18% from 2025 levels by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040. Current national plans would cut emissions by only 5% to 8% by 2030 and 11% to 15% by 2035.
The report projected global warming of 2.8 deg C by 2100 under current policies, or 2.6 deg C if countries fully implement existing climate pledges. Both estimates are higher than the 2025 projections, reflecting the US withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and revised assessments of historical emissions.
As countries prepare for the next round of climate talks in Turkey, COP31, UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres said it was crucial not to give up on efforts to rein in the emissions that are fuelling floods, fires and other natural disasters.
“Overshoot is not surrender. We can still keep it as small and as short as possible – and bring temperatures back below 1.5 deg C by the end of the century,” he said.
Under the 2015 Paris Agreement, countries agreed to try to keep the average temperature increase at well below 2 deg C and ideally 1.5 deg C.
As limiting warming to 1.5 deg C with no or limited overshoot was no longer considered possible, the UN Environment Programme said its new "lowest possible" overshoot scenario gives roughly a 50% chance that temperatures could return to 1.5 deg C or below by 2100.
The report said climate plans submitted since 2025 had made virtually no difference to future warming projections, and that returning to 1.5 deg C would depend on large-scale carbon removal, the feasibility of which was uncertain. REUTERS

Al Carns asks how Britain will organise for drone war
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
06:00:48 BST
14:00:48 KST

Britain’s response to the uncrewed formations being stood up in the United States, Germany and Ukraine runs through the hybrid Navy and the investment going into innovation and drone technology, the Defence Secretary told the Commons, according to an answer given in Parliament.
Al Carns, the Labour member for Birmingham Selly Oak, a Royal Marines officer who served as Minister for Veterans and People until earlier this year, set three allied examples against the British position and asked what would change in the structure of the armed forces.
Carns said: “Drones are changing the way we fight. How are we changing the structures as to how we fight? America is creating the robotic Uncrewed Systems Combatant Command. Germany has created uncrewed regiment. The Ukrainians have created unmanned systems force. What projects are we moving forward to really revolutionise this, into the Army, Navy and Air Force?”
Wes Streeting, the Secretary of State for Defence, thanked Carns for the leadership he showed on the subject as a minister and for the advice he continues to give, before naming the hybrid Navy and the heavy investment going into innovation and drone technology as the vehicles for the change. He said: “We have to be ready for the fight ahead.” Being ready, he went on, means out innovating as well as out producing, and building new systems and new platforms.
Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces were created by presidential decree in 2024 and stood up as a branch in their own right alongside the ground forces, air force and navy, giving drone units their own command chain, procurement route and recruitment pipeline. Germany and the United States have since moved along similar lines, folding uncrewed systems into formations and commands with budgets attached to them.
Britain has taken the programme route so far, and the hybrid Navy that Streeting named covers four uncrewed classes and one crewed one, with Type 91 as an uncrewed missile platform, Type 92 an uncrewed underwater sensing platform, Type 93 an extra-large uncrewed underwater vessel and Type 94 an uncrewed radar platform, sitting alongside a future Common Combat Vessel.
The Defence Investment Plan put at least £1.3 billion behind the construct when the designations were announced earlier this year, and the department told Parliament this month that planning assumptions support progressive introduction from the early 2030s with no service entry dates yet set.

A TH18-style endgame village — where more players than ever are starting their Clash of Clans story in 2026
What Town Hall 18 Actually Brought to the Table
TH18 launched on November 17, 2025, and it was one of those rare updates that rewrites how a base fundamentally works. The headline feature is the Guardian system. Instead of one fixed Town Hall weapon that every attacker on the planet already knows how to handle, you now pick a Guardian — a special defender tailored to your base. Suddenly there is no single right answer for hitting a TH18, and war attacks have become noticeably harder to three-star. For defenders, it is the most fun the game has felt in years.
The Revenge Tower earned its fan club within a week. It fights back harder as your base takes damage, so the worse your defense is going, the more it punishes an attacker who overcommits. Add the Super Wizard Tower, the Meteor Golem smashing its way through walls as a heavy new elixir troop, and the Totem Spell that drops a tanky decoy to distract and stun defenses, and you get the biggest defensive shake-up Clash of Clans has seen in years.
And Supercell isn't done. The February 2026 update stacked fresh levels onto TH18 defenses like the Giga Bomb and Seeking Air Mine, while the August update brought a new Pet, extra Supercharge tiers and Hero Journey tweaks. The full breakdown lives in Supercell's official release notes if you want the fine print.
Town Hall 18 at a glance: six additions that changed how bases defend — and how attacks fail — in 2026
Why the Grind Got Heavier, Not Lighter
Here is the part the update trailers don't show you. TH18 didn't just add content — it added time. Every new defense level, hero level and wall tier is builder hours, and the Hero Journey track introduced in June 2026 made hero levels more valuable than ever. Every hero level in your Home Village now earns points toward ore chests, Epic Hero Equipment and exclusive skins. Sounds generous — until you remember heroes were already the slowest upgrades in the game, with a single top-end upgrade locking a hero away for days at a stretch. Now skipping them costs you rewards on top of progress.
For a player sitting at TH14 or TH15, a comfortable TH18 account looks like this: months of laboratory time, a wall grind measured in hundreds of pieces, hero upgrades chained back to back, and a completely new defensive meta to learn the moment you arrive. And unlike earlier Town Halls, you can't hide behind one carry hero anymore — the Hero Journey track wants all of them leveling together. None of it is impossible. But if you have a job, classes, or other games you actually enjoy, it starts to feel like a second job that doesn't pay.
The Catch-Up Roadmap That Actually Works
If you're taking the grind head-on, order matters more than effort. The players who reach TH18 fastest run roughly the same five-step sequence — you'll see the same pattern in every serious progression thread this year:
Max offense first. Army camps, laboratory level and the armies you actually use. A stronger army farms faster, and faster farming funds everything else on this list.
Keep heroes on permanent duty. Idle heroes are a double loss in 2026 — missed progress and missed Hero Journey points. Time your Books of Heroes and hammers around war schedules so nothing sits still.
Ride the Hero Journey. It rewards hero levels you were grinding anyway with ore, gear and skins. Free value on top of mandatory work — collect it.
Spend CWL medals and event currency before they expire. League medals and event rewards convert into magic items and hammers that skip entire upgrade timers — days off your queue in one click.
Save walls and Supercharge for last. They are the status layer of the game. They matter, but they don't gate your progression the way the lab and heroes do.
Follow that order and the climb stops feeling like chaos. It becomes a schedule.

When Buying an Account Is the Sensible Move
Even a perfect roadmap can't manufacture time. Some players simply don't have a year of builder queues in them, and it's more honest to say that out loud: buying a Clash of Clans account is a shortcut, and a shortcut trades money for time. Supercell's terms don't recognize account trading, so the risk was never the game itself — it's picking the wrong seller. Nearly every horror story starts the same way: a random chat seller who keeps the recovery email, a self-appointed middleman who vanishes mid-deal, or an account reclaimed weeks after payment.
That's why experienced buyers stick to established stores. A shop like QuickGameShop has built its name on verified stats, secure Supercell ID handovers and support that still answers after the payment clears — which is what separates a purchase from a gamble. Check the hero levels, look at war stars, ask exactly how the transfer works, and only accept guarantees that are put in writing. Do that, and the shortcut behaves like a shortcut instead of a story you regret telling.
The Bottom Line
Town Hall 18 made Clash of Clans feel new again — fresh defenses, a shifting meta and a progression system that finally pays you for the grind you were doing anyway. It also stretched the climb. Love the journey? The roadmap above will save you real months. Rather spend your evenings attacking than watching builders? A verified account puts you in TH18 wars this weekend instead of next year. Lula, Bolsonaro seek to disqualify each other ahead of Brazil runoff
Both candidates for the Brazilian presidency have called for the disqualification of their rivals over allegations of social media interference, ramping up political drama ahead of the close-fought October 25 runoff election.
Brazil’s right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has requested the annulment of the candidacy of his rival, President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, over what he called unlawful propaganda.
Lawyers for Bolsonaro filed a request with the Superior Electoral Court on Tuesday, alleging Lula’s “abuse of power” in the mass dissemination of government postings during the campaign period via WhatsApp.
Bolsonaro’s camp claimed the Brazilian government sent mass messages to millions of Brazilians via the messaging service, promoting social programmes, benefits and government initiatives in the midst of the presidential race, Brazilian media reported.
The request to the electoral court seeks to declare Lula and Social Communications Minister Sidonio Palmeira ineligible to hold public office for a period of eight years.
‘Algorithmic manipulation’
In the other camp, Lula’s campaign said on Tuesday that it would request the disqualification of Bolsonaro on Wednesday over alleged election interference by WhatsApp parent company, the tech giant Meta.
Lula’s petition, which has yet to be officially filed, alleges “algorithmic manipulation” by Meta aimed at harming Lula’s chances of winning, a campaign source told AFP.
The electoral court had given Meta 24 hours on Monday to prove it was complying with an order to treat both campaigns equally, threatening a daily fine of around $200,000 if it didn’t.
The order came after Lula’s campaign alleged that Meta, which owns Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram, was suppressing his online content to boost Bolsonaro.
“We have completed the implementation of the measures to comply with the Superior Electoral Court’s decision,” the company said on Tuesday.
Lula and Bolsonaro are locked in a heated presidential race after the right-wing candidate, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, won the initial round of voting earlier this month with 47 percent of the vote to the incumbent’s 45 percent.
Polls show a very close race ahead of Sunday’s runoff round.

'Troubling pattern': UN experts flag 'use of excessive force' during India protests
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
04:53:57 UTC
13:53:57 KST

A protestor is detained by the police during a youth demonstration demanding the resignation of the country's election chief Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India
NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday asserted that human rights should not be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective targeting of countries, opposing attempts to turn allegations and incomplete statistics into a “negative characterisation” of the world's largest democracy.While speaking at UNGA Third Committee, deputy secretary in the ministry of external affairs Barkha Tamrakar said, "Human rights not to be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective country targeting."
"India engages with international human rights mechanisms, but such engagement must be based on dialogue, consultation, cooperation with non-selectivity and transparency as guiding principle," she added."We call on delegations to cite the report faithfully, not to inflate a humanitarian communication into a verdict."She also opposed any "attempt to convert unverified allegations, incomplete statistics or a report that contains no India country observation into a negative characterisation of the world's largest democracy".
Remarks come amid UN experts’ concerns over protestsTamrakar's remarks came amid concerns raised by UN human rights experts over recent youth-led protests in New Delhi.
On Tuesday, more than 20 UN human rights experts in Geneva expressed alarm over what they described as a “repeatedly heavy-handed police response” to peaceful youth-led demonstrations in the national capital.In a statement shared by UN special procedures, the experts alleged that law enforcement agencies had used force against unarmed students, detained protesters arbitrarily and imposed broad restrictions on public gatherings. They called on Indian authorities to respect the right to peaceful assembly and ensure accountability for alleged abuses.“Despite the non-violent nature of the assemblies, law enforcement has deployed force against unarmed students,” the experts said.
UN experts flag mass detentions, alleged ill-treatmentThe experts said hundreds of thousands of students and their supporters had gathered peacefully across the country to protest government decisions concerning the education system and, more recently, voter-roll deletions.They referred to reports that the deletions affected 130 million individuals, reportedly belonging to Muslim, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities.According to the statement, more than 7,000 young people, journalists, human rights defenders, lawyers and political party members were recently detained in New Delhi and taken to detention centres farther away. Their phones were allegedly seized and protest-related material deleted. Most were released after 24 hours, including protest leaders, the experts said.The statement also cited reports of injuries and ill-treatment among protesters, expressing particular concern over allegations of sexual violence and other forms of gender-based abuse during demonstrations and related detentions.
The experts also raised concerns over the reported use of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) to impose broad restrictions on public gatherings, suspend public transportation and enforce internet shutdowns.They said restrictions on peaceful assembly must be lawful, pursue a legitimate objective and be necessary and proportionate.They urged Indian authorities to immediately stop the excessive use of force, lift blanket restrictions on assemblies and refrain from the misuse of digital surveillance, including biometric monitoring and internet disruptions.The UN experts called for an independent, impartial and thorough investigation into the conduct of law enforcement personnel and affiliated forces, urging authorities to ensure accountability, justice and reparations for victims.

Currently with The Times of India, she covers public policy, politics and global affairs. She is particularly drawn to human-interest stories that put people at the heart of an issue, spark awareness , and contribute to meaningful conversations.

Motorcycle Valve Clearance: Symptoms & Adjustment Mistakes
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
04:47:49 UTC
13:47:49 KST

A motorcycle engine depends on precise timing between its valves and other moving components. Valve clearance, also known as valve lash, is the small gap specified between components in the valve train when the valves are in the appropriate closed position. Although this gap may seem insignificant, incorrect clearance can affect engine performance, starting behavior, noise, and long-term reliability.
Understanding how valve clearance works helps motorcycle owners recognize potential problems and helps technicians perform more accurate engine maintenance.
What Is Motorcycle Valve Clearance?
Valve clearance allows for thermal expansion as the engine heats up during operation. The correct gap depends on the engine design and the manufacturer's specifications.
If the clearance is too tight or too loose, the valve train may not operate as intended. The adjustment method also varies by motorcycle. Some engines use screw-and-locknut adjusters, while others use shims or different mechanical arrangements.
For this reason, technicians should always consult the service manual for the specific motorcycle rather than applying a universal clearance measurement.
Common Symptoms of Incorrect Valve Clearance
1. Unusual Noise From the Engine
Excessive valve clearance can sometimes produce a noticeable ticking or tapping sound from the cylinder head. However, not every ticking noise indicates a valve adjustment problem. Camshaft components, timing chains, lubrication issues, and other mechanical parts can produce similar sounds.
A technician should inspect the engine systematically instead of assuming that noise alone confirms incorrect clearance.
2. Difficult Cold Starting
When valve clearance becomes too tight, a valve may not fully seat under certain operating conditions. This can reduce cylinder sealing and make starting more difficult.
Cold-starting problems can also result from battery weakness, ignition faults, fuel delivery issues, or incorrect fuel mixture. Measuring valve clearance is therefore one possible diagnostic step, not an automatic solution.
3. Reduced Engine Performance
Incorrect valve clearance can affect valve operation and combustion efficiency. Depending on the engine and the severity of the problem, the rider may notice reduced power, rough running, or changes in engine response.
If a motorcycle loses performance, technicians should also consider compression, ignition timing, air intake restrictions, and fuel system operation before identifying the cause.
4. Poor Idle Quality
An engine with incorrect valve clearance may run unevenly, particularly if valve sealing or cylinder performance is affected. However, unstable idle speed is also associated with intake leaks, dirty throttle bodies, fuel system problems, and sensor faults on fuel-injected motorcycles.
Accurate diagnosis requires checking the symptoms against the engine's actual condition. Technicians investigating electronic fuel delivery or sensor-related faults can also explore specialized motorcycle EFI and diagnostic training to learn more about electronic troubleshooting.
What Causes Valve Clearance to Change?
Valve clearance can change gradually as engine components wear and operating conditions affect the valve train. Valve seat recession, wear at contact surfaces, and other mechanical changes may alter the original gap.
The direction of the change depends on the engine design and the components involved. In some engines, clearance may decrease over time, making periodic inspection especially important even when the engine does not produce unusual noise.
Maintenance intervals differ between motorcycles. Following the manufacturer's service schedule is the most reliable way to determine when inspection is required.
How Is Valve Clearance Checked and Adjusted?
A proper inspection starts with identifying the correct specifications and allowing the engine to reach the temperature required by the service procedure, commonly a cold engine unless the manufacturer specifies otherwise.
The technician then accesses the valve train, positions the crankshaft at the specified timing mark, and measures the gap using the appropriate method, often a feeler gauge.
If the measurement falls outside the specified range, the adjustment procedure depends on the engine design. Screw-adjusted systems may require loosening a locknut and repositioning an adjuster. Shim-operated systems may require selecting the correct replacement shim based on the measured clearance and the manufacturer's procedure.
After adjustment, the measurements should be checked again. The engine should then be reassembled correctly and inspected for leaks, abnormal noise, and proper operation.
Because incorrect adjustment can cause serious engine damage, inexperienced technicians should follow the service manual and obtain appropriate supervision.
Why Practical Motorcycle Repair Skills Matter
Valve adjustment is only one part of motorcycle engine maintenance. A capable technician must also understand compression, lubrication, ignition, fuel delivery, and the relationship between mechanical components.
Developing these skills requires more than memorizing procedures. Practical learning helps technicians use measuring tools correctly, recognize abnormal wear, follow manufacturer specifications, and distinguish between similar symptoms caused by different faults.
People who want to develop these abilities can explore professional motorcycle repair training to learn more about motorcycle inspection, maintenance, mechanical systems, and troubleshooting.
Conclusion
Incorrect motorcycle valve clearance can contribute to engine noise, difficult starting, poor performance, and other operating problems. However, these symptoms can have several causes, making accurate measurement and systematic diagnosis essential.
By following manufacturer specifications, inspecting the valve train correctly, and verifying every adjustment, technicians can help maintain engine reliability and avoid unnecessary repairs. For motorcycle owners and aspiring mechanics alike, understanding valve clearance is an important part of learning how motorcycle engines operate.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Randall G. Schriver, chair of the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, expressed concern about Chinese coast guard patrols in waters east of Taiwan at an international symposium Tuesday.
The patrols appear to be gray-zone activities, with vessels ostensibly conducting law enforcement operations, Schriver said, per CNA. He said these activities advance China’s sovereignty claims and form part of its broader legal, political, and intelligence warfare, potentially destabilizing the region.
Schriver said that if a fishing boat were in distress east of Taiwan and Chinese vessels arrived first to rescue it, observers might view the operation as a humanitarian effort. China would, however, be exercising the authority of a sovereign state, reinforcing its claim to be the legitimate sovereign authority in the eyes of domestic and international audiences, he said.
Such scenarios should be considered in defense deterrence planning and operational concepts, Schriver said, according to CNA. He welcomed the American Institute in Taiwan’s publication of photographs of Taiwan’s coast guard, but said effective operational responses to China’s emerging challenges were also needed.
He suggested that Taiwan and Japan could cooperate on anti-blockade exercises between Keelung and Yonaguni Island and develop operational concepts to counter potential Chinese coercion.
Schriver emphasized the importance of ongoing military training between Taiwan and the US, describing it as a mechanism that took considerable time to establish, per CNA. He said its impact extends beyond improving military capabilities to strengthening morale and professionalism.
Having observed the training in classrooms and at exercise facilities, Schriver said Taiwanese service members appeared to feel they were receiving high-quality training tailored to real-world operational requirements. This significantly boosted their morale and confidence, he said.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Four workers died after falling from a steel structure during a construction accident at TSMC’s Fab 22 site in Kaohsiung on Tuesday, prompting an investigation into a suspected bolt failure.
The accident occurred at about 4:53 p.m. at the company’s construction site in the Southern Taiwan Science Park. The four workers were employed by contractor Shanghao Machinery and were performing steel-structure hoisting and installation work when they fell from the third floor along with steel components, per UDN.
Three workers died on Tuesday evening despite emergency treatment. The fourth, a 37-year-old surnamed Huang (黃), was taken to Kaohsiung Veterans General Hospital for emergency surgery and intensive care but died on Wednesday morning, bringing the death toll to four.
Preliminary findings suggest that bolts on a connecting plate of the third-floor exterior steel structure may have broken, causing the workers and steel components to fall. All four workers were wearing safety harnesses, but the collapse of the structure prevented their safety ropes from functioning properly. Authorities said the exact cause remains under investigation.
Labor inspectors were dispatched to the site after the accident and ordered steel-structure hoisting work suspended at the project. Investigators will examine the connecting plates, bolts, hoisting procedures, and compliance with occupational safety regulations before determining responsibility and possible penalties, per CNA.
TSMC said the accident occurred in a construction area contracted to an outside company. Its on-site safety team was cooperating with authorities and assisting the contractor with follow-up arrangements.
TSMC also announced that it had voluntarily suspended steel-structure work at its construction sites nationwide while reviewing the incident and cooperating with the investigation.
The science park administration said the accident’s impact on the Fab 22 construction schedule would depend on construction and operational arrangements, which are the responsibility of TSMC and its contractors.

Why is Hong Kong so hot in October and will winter be warmer than usual?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
04:40:37 UTC
13:40:37 KST

Why is Hong Kong so hot in October and will winter be warmer than usual?
Climate expert Amos Tai says Hong Kong’s autumn heat stems from three factors, with above-normal temperatures likely to persist
Hong Kong’s exceptionally warm October weather is being driven by a combination of a super typhoon, El Nino and global warming, a climate expert has said, warning that higher-than-usual temperatures are likely to persist through the winter.
The warning came as autumn temperatures across the city topped 30 degrees Celsius (86 Fahrenheit) over the past few weeks.
Professor Amos Tai Pui-kuen, of the earth and environmental sciences department at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, explained on Wednesday that El Nino had altered typhoon paths and weakened the northeasterly winds that typically reached the city in autumn.
“A ‘super’ El Nino means that paths of typhoons would move more northerly … if and when typhoons do hit Hong Kong, because of the high sea level temperatures, there will be more heat and steam evaporating, which contributes to a stronger typhoon, too,” he said.

The operation was ultimately shelved because of Trump's opposition, although both leaders have continued threatening renewed military action against Tehran. In a video released Monday from an Israeli air base, Netanyahu told Trump that they had unfinished business to complete together. Trump responded by praising the Israeli prime minister and expressing confidence in their partnership.
According to the FT, current and former Israeli security officials fear that a new war launched so close to the election could undermine the democratic process. The Orionid meteor shower peaks this week. Here's the best time to watch
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
04:30:12 UTC
13:30:12 KST

In Brief
- The Orionid meteor shower is forecast to peak early Thursday morning, up until Saturday.
- A bright moon may wash out many meteors, with the best viewing before dawn.
Keen stargazers hoping to catch a glimpse of the Orionid meteor shower this week may need to set an early alarm — and lower their expectations.
The annual meteor shower, caused by debris left behind by Halley's Comet, graces our skies every October and is expected to peak in the early hours of Thursday morning.
But a bright moon may dampen this year's shower, though astronomers say patient sky watchers could still catch meteors streaking across the pre-dawn sky.
"This year will probably be a quiet one," University of Southern Queensland astronomer Jonti Horner said.
News that makes sense
Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.
What is the Orionid meteor shower?
The Orionid meteor shower occurs each October as Earth passes through a stream of debris left behind by Halley's Comet.
Halley’s Comet is a famous comet of ice and dust that orbits the sun every 75 to 76 years. It will next be visible from Earth in mid-2061.
This year's shower coincides with the Northern and Southern Taurid meteor showers, which contribute a handful of extra meteors to the night sky.
The different showers can often be distinguished by their speed.
Orionids streak quickly across the sky, while Taurids tend to move much more slowly.
"If you are up in the early hours of the morning before sunrise and you see a meteor and it's quite slow, that was probably a Taurid," Horner said. "If you see one that was really fast, that was probably an Orionid."
The shower also has a remarkably long history.
Horner said the Orionids have been observed for at least 2,500 years, with some reports believed to date back to around 800 BC.
Why this year's display may be quieter
Under ideal conditions, the Orionids normally produce about 20 to 30 meteors an hour.
But those figures assume dark skies, clear weather and little interference from moonlight.
This year, a bright waxing gibbous moon is expected to wash out many of the faint meteors.
"The moon doesn't set until 2 or 3am," Horner said. "While the moon's high in the sky, there's a lot more light pollution, which hides all but the brightest meteors."
Horner said moonlight could reduce the number of visible meteors by as much as half, particularly before the moon drops below the horizon.
"What that means is that I would not be suggesting to anybody that they go out until the moon has set."
When is the best time to watch?
Anyone hoping to catch the shower should look to the skies in the hours before dawn.
The Orionids are effectively invisible before midnight because the point in the sky from which they appear to emerge, known as the radiant, has not yet risen high enough above the horizon.
The best viewing window on Thursday morning is expected to be between 3am and 4am (AEDT).
"Wednesday night is formally forecast to be the best night, but there's a little bit of uncertainty in that because the numbers wiggle around up and down," Horner said.
"I'd say basically anytime this week, even as far as Friday or Saturday, you've got a chance of getting reasonable numbers, but the moon is getting worse, not better."
City viewers may still be able to spot the same bright meteors folks in the rural areas will see.
"The brighter meteors, you'll see whether you're in the city or in the country, so long as you're away from direct streetlights."
But he said there were no guarantees you'll actually see any meteors.
"If you're someone getting up early, getting up before dawn and you're having your morning coffee, going and sitting out under the stars, you might get to see something and that'll be nice."
A warm-up for December
Anyone disappointed by this week's display won't have to wait long for another celestial show.
Horner describes the Orionids as more of a warm-up act for December's Geminid meteor shower, widely regarded as the year's best.
While the Orionids typically produce around 20 to 30 meteors an hour under ideal conditions, the Geminids can generate as many as 150.
"The Geminids are everything the Orionids are not," Horner said. "They're much stronger, much better, and the moon's out of the way."
The Geminids are expected to peak around 14 December, with strong viewing conditions forecast either side of the peak.
Horner's advice for that shower? Use your annual leave.
"I would actually be planning a camping trip and getting somewhere dark for the Geminids," he said.
And if this year's Orionids leave you underwhelmed, there seem to be only two real alternatives: a time machine, or a lot of patience.
"The Orionids were probably a lot better around 500 BC than they are now," Horner said.
"But there are some predictions that the Orionids could actually be very spectacular in the year 2070."

New EU Arctic strategy promises closer cooperation with Greenland
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
04:18:22 UTC
13:18:22 KST

The European Commission wants to strengthen ties with Greenland through increased investment and cooperation on energy, infrastructure and security.
The plans are outlined in a new Arctic strategy presented Tuesday.
“There is no doubt that this Arctic strategy shows that we are in the process of tying the EU and Greenland closer to each other for mutual benefit and in mutual respect,” said EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen.
The announcement follows European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s visit to Greenland in September.
During the visit, she signed a cooperation agreement with Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen and Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen.
The agreement included 1.5 billion DKK in EU investment, partly for Greenland’s digital infrastructure.
Jørgensen said the EU also intends to cooperate with Greenland on green energy.
However, Nielsen has made clear that Greenland is not seeking EU membership.
Jørgensen emphasized that the strategy respects Greenland’s right to determine its own future.
“From the EU’s side, we are committed to forging close ties, but the question of independence is decided by Denmark and Greenland,” he said.
He added that EU funding would not impose conditions restricting Greenland’s future decisions.
The strategy also recognizes a recent agreement between Greenland, Denmark and the United States aimed at strengthening Arctic security.
Proposals include expanding Europe’s icebreaker fleet, establishing a maritime security center and creating a facility to monitor undersea cables.
The Commission also wants more secure cable connections to Greenland and greater use of renewable energy in communities currently dependent on diesel generators.
Jørgensen said the measures reflect the EU’s commitment to Greenland as an important partner.

The figure marks a sharp increase from August 10, when the department reported more than 175,000 revocations.
“With over 300,000 revocations, the Trump administration has revoked more visas at a faster pace than any previous administration,” State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott wrote on X.
He said the U.S. would not tolerate visa holders breaking laws, committing fraud or threatening national security.
Trump has defended his stricter immigration policies, including deportations, as necessary to improve security.
However, human rights organizations have criticized the administration’s approach, arguing that it has violated due process rights and freedom of speech while creating uncertainty, particularly among ethnic minorities.
Several cases involving foreign nationals who participated in pro-Palestinian demonstrations against Israel’s military operations in Gaza have drawn criticism after their visas were revoked.
Other cases have involved foreign nationals losing visas over social media comments about the killing of conservative activist Charlie Kirk.
The administration has also increased scrutiny of immigrants’ and visa applicants’ social media activity.
Human rights groups argue that national security concerns have been used to justify targeting government critics and certain immigrant communities.
Trump campaigned in 2024 on promises to curb illegal immigration.
His administration has also introduced restrictions affecting legal immigration, including higher fees for certain work visas.
The State Department has not provided a breakdown of the reasons behind the more than 300,000 visa revocations.

====================================================================================================

Share of 21-year-olds living at home in Denmark nearly doubles since 2011
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
04:18:11 UTC
13:18:11 KST

Denmark’s power grid operator will answer hundreds of connection requests in November while big data centers face long delays.
Energinet, the Danish state-owned electricity transmission company, has now mapped out the capacity needs on the country’s strained electricity grid, the company said in a press release on Wednesday.
With this overview finished, the company will be able to answer applications from several hundred electricity consumers and power producers in November about whether they can connect to the grid.
“In a time of sharply rising demand for electricity, we unfortunately cannot give connection to everyone at the pace they desire,” said Soren Dupont Kristensen, the acting chief executive officer of Energinet.
“But there is room in the transmission grid to cover the electricity needs of ordinary households, smaller businesses, and critical societal functions such as healthcare, defense, and emergency preparedness, both now and in the years to come,” Kristensen said.
Customers will be sorted into four priority categories that were recently passed by a broad political majority as part of an emergency plan for the power network.
Projects placed in Category 1 and Category 2 will get their answers first. These two groups include critical public services, as well as green transition and electrification projects.
Category 3 includes energy storage systems, such as large battery facilities. Category 4 covers major electricity users, including data centers.
“We do not have all the results in place, but it looks difficult to give full grid access to projects in categories 3 and 4,” Kristensen said in Wednesday’s statement.
The political emergency plan was designed to let Energinet and local electricity companies choose who gets hooked up to the power lines. Under this plan, large data centers are pushed to the back of the line because the grid does not have room for huge new projects.
Energinet has faced heavy criticism for expanding the Danish electricity network too slowly. This criticism has come from several groups, including Rigsrevisionen, the National Audit Office of Denmark.
In March, the state company stopped connecting new projects. At that time, Energinet announced that no new connection contracts would be signed until the autumn.
In May, the company stated that very large connection projects could face waiting times of five to ten years. At that point, Energinet also admitted that demand for power had grown at an unexpectedly rapid speed.
Several business groups say it is good news that applicants will soon get answers, but they stress that Denmark still has a real shortage of space on its power grid.
This warning came from DI, Dansk Industri, the Confederation of Danish Industry, which is the main employers’ and business association in Denmark; Dansk Erhverv, the Danish Chamber of Commerce, an employers’ organization representing businesses; and Green Power Denmark, the business and trade group for the green energy sector.
Ulrich Bang, the deputy director for climate, energy, environment, and building at Dansk Erhverv, said the likely lack of space for Category 3 and Category 4 projects shows how serious the situation is.
“Denmark cannot build the industries, business community, and jobs of the future in a waiting room,” Bang said.
“Therefore, action must be taken now, and we look forward to dialogue with authorities and grid companies on how room can be made for more on the electricity grid in the very short term,” Bang said.

Plans to tighten Denmark’s senior pension rules dropped after political opposition
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
04:17:52 UTC
13:17:52 KST

The government has abandoned proposed changes to Denmark’s senior pension scheme after failing to secure support from parties behind the existing agreement.
Employment Minister Ane Halsboe-Jørgensen announced the decision Tuesday following a meeting with the parties involved.
The changes were part of the government’s proposed 2027 budget and were expected to save 200 million DKK in 2028, 500 million DKK in 2029 and 800 million DKK in 2030.
Under the proposal, applicants would have needed to prove that their ability to work was limited to 15 hours a week or less across all types of jobs, rather than just their most recent job.
This would have made qualifying for senior pension more difficult. In 2026, a single person receiving senior pension gets 22,053 DKK per month.
The scheme was introduced through a political agreement in 2019. Its signatories include the Danish People’s Party, the Social Democrats, the Socialist People’s Party, the Moderates and the Social Liberal Party.
Changes to the agreement require approval from all participating parties during the parliamentary term.
Several center-right parties opposed the proposal, while the Red-Green Alliance also rejected changes.
“We respect the agreements we have. It has not been my intention to terminate any agreement,” Halsboe-Jørgensen said.
“On the contrary. The fact that I called the colleagues from the other parties together today was precisely an expression of the fact that I actually wanted to discuss it with them, and that I respect that the agreement we have with each other gives all of them a veto right against changes in this area,” she added.
Dropping the proposal leaves a gap in the government’s budget plans.
Halsboe-Jørgensen said spending priorities would need to change but did not specify where the missing funds would come from.
Finance Minister Peter Hummelgaard will now have to address the shortfall during negotiations on the 2027 Finance Act.

New partnership aims to connect lonely patients with social activities through their GPs
A new partnership in Denmark aims to help people experiencing loneliness and social isolation access community activities through referrals from their general practitioners.
Many people visit their doctors because they feel lonely, but their needs cannot always be addressed through medical treatment, said David Vincent Nielsen, a loneliness consultant at Ældre Sagen, a Danish association for older people, and chairman of Folkebevægelsen mod Ensomhed, a national movement against loneliness.
“There are a lot of people who seek out the healthcare and care system because they experience loneliness and social isolation.
“Most often, they cannot get help from the healthcare system because they need companionship and social relationships,” he said.
Under the proposed system, a doctor could issue a social referral for a patient. A professional or volunteer would then contact the patient and help identify activities and community groups suited to their needs.
The professional, known as a bridge-builder, would discuss the patient’s situation and help them find relevant offers from local organizations and municipalities.
These could include knitting groups, card game clubs or local exercise groups. Patients could also be encouraged to become volunteers themselves.
Nielsen said many people experiencing loneliness face barriers that make it difficult for them to seek out social activities and build relationships on their own.
For social referrals to become a regular part of Denmark’s health care system, however, the public sector would need to fund the service, he said.
“In 2017, the University of Southern Denmark calculated that loneliness cost 5.5 billion kroner, but since then, the prevalence of loneliness has increased by 42 percent, so around 10 billion kroner would be a qualified estimate today,” Nielsen said.
He argued that social referrals could also help reduce health care costs by addressing loneliness before people repeatedly seek medical assistance.
“But social referrals will not necessarily be an expense. Right now, there are at least 500,000 extra visits to general practice each year that are due to loneliness and paid for by the regions,” he said.
Pilot projects are already underway, Nielsen said. The new partnership aims to bring the existing efforts together into a coordinated model that could eventually be introduced nationwide.
The World Health Organization recognizes social referrals as a way to connect people with nonmedical support. According to the organization, one in five doctor visits is prompted by problems that cannot be resolved through clinical treatment.
The United Kingdom was the first country to incorporate social referrals into its health care policy. The WHO says there are now 3,300 active bridge-builders in the country.
The Danish partnership brings together Ældre Sagen, the Danish Red Cross, Social Sundhed, DGI, Sund By Netværket, Not a Box, and Frivilligcentre og Selvhjælp Danmark, an organization representing volunteer centers and self-help initiatives in Denmark.

Danish municipalities shut down IT systems after potential security risk
Kombit, the IT organization serving Denmark’s municipalities, has shut down several of its digital services, either fully or partially, after identifying a potential technical security risk.
The shutdown began Wednesday afternoon and affects services including Aula, the digital communication platform used by schools and parents, and the municipal library system, Lars Skov Granerud, Kombit’s press manager, told news agency Ritzau.
“We have been made aware of a potential technical security risk in an underlying element of several of our solutions,” he said.
“Therefore, we decided a short while ago to shut down several of them.”

The disruption also affects several municipal systems used by local government employees in their daily work, including systems for processing benefit payments.
Aula has been shut down completely, while the library system is only partially affected, Granerud said.
Kombit has not disclosed which other digital services have been affected.
Unauthorized people have gained access to parts of the computer systems of the Danish department store chain.
Magasin reported the incident in an email to DR, the Danish public broadcaster.
Following the breach, Magasin warned members of its customer loyalty club, named Goodie, that their personal details may have been compromised. The exposed data includes names, addresses, and purchase history.
“We are working dedicatedly with external experts to handle the incident, including re-establishing our access to the systems. In addition, we have reported the incident to both the police and Datatilsynet,” Magasin stated in the email. Datatilsynet is the Danish Data Protection Agency, the national authority that oversees data privacy rules.
Magasin warned that the compromised details could be used to make phishing scams look more believable.
Phishing is a deceptive practice where scammers try to trick individuals into handing over personal information. This often happens through fake emails designed to steal login details for MitID, the official digital identification system used across Denmark for banking and public services.
Magasin stressed in its message to club members that the security breach did not include any credit card information.
“We want to emphasize that we are working to limit the scope of the breach and to ensure that something similar does not happen again,” the email said.
The incident follows a similar alert sent to shoppers a few weeks ago by the British online retailer Asos.
In that case, Asos stated that an unauthorized person managed to enter an employee account. The intruder used that account to pull information from external platforms that Asos works with.
That breach allowed the unauthorized user to access customer names and contact details.
Following the incident, Asos told its customers to be cautious of unexpected phone calls and messages from individuals pretending to work for the company. Asos also reported its security breach to the police.
Foreign workers and older employees fuel Denmark’s job market growth
The Danish labor market added 3,600 wage earners in August, according to a report published Wednesday morning by Danmarks Statistik, the national statistical authority of Denmark.
The increase follows a July that showed signs of a small slowdown.
The new numbers support the view held by financial group Nykredit that the Danish job market remains active.
Palle Sørensen, who serves as chief economist at Nykredit, noted that the trend is clear over a longer period.
“It is completely clear when you look at the development over a slightly longer horizon. In the past 12 months alone, there have been 29,638 more wage earners,” Sørensen said in a written comment.
He added that the job market matches the general economy.
“The development in the labor market matches well with the general economic development. Activity is increasing, and it is therefore not surprising that more people are entering employment,” Sørensen said.
There are multiple reasons for the increase in employed people.
One of the main reasons is foreign labor, according to Jesper Grunnet-Lauridsen. He works as chief analyst at 3F, Fagligt Fælles Forbund, which is the United Federation of Danish Workers and the largest trade union in Denmark.
“An important explanation is that more foreign employees have arrived, at the same time as more seniors are staying longer in the labor market,” Grunnet-Lauridsen said in a written comment.
He explained that these groups have helped employers find staff.
“This has made it possible for employment to continue to rise without companies having a correspondingly harder time finding employees,” Grunnet-Lauridsen said.
Neither Nykredit nor 3F expects the Danish labor market to slow down in the near future.
Sørensen said that recent experience shows that later retirement and foreign workers make the size of the total workforce more flexible.
“This is somewhat of an innovation compared to previously, where employment growth was often assumed to be temporary,” Sørensen said.

The payment company Nets has lost a court case against Konkurrencerådet, the Danish Competition Council, which serves as the public competition authority in Denmark.
The ruling was delivered Wednesday by Sø- og Handelsretten, the Danish Maritime and Commercial Court.
Nets had asked the court to set aside a decision made by the Competition Council. That decision concluded that Nets abused its dominant position in the market for payment solutions between the years 2012 and 2016.
The case involves the company Teller, which was a subsidiary under Nets during that period. Teller offered what were described as exclusivity discounts to a number of large customers. The competition authorities determined that this practice broke legal rules meant to secure free competition, and they made their official decision on the case back in 2018.
The legal process has taken several years. Alongside the civil lawsuit, police have also run an investigation into Nets. That investigation led to criminal charges against the company, with authorities seeking a fine. The criminal case was put on hold to wait for the result of the civil case, and it has not yet gone to trial.
The specific legal reasons behind the court decision are not yet known. In a brief summary published on its website, the Maritime and Commercial Court stated that the full ruling will be released within four weeks.
The court noted that the delay is needed because the text of the ruling may contain business secrets that cannot be made public.
Share of 21-year-olds living at home in Denmark nearly doubles since 2011
More young adults in Denmark are choosing to stay in their family homes, with the share of 21-year-olds living with their parents rising from 32 percent in 2011 to 57 percent in 2025.
The figures come from Statistics Denmark and are highlighted in a new study by Realdania, a Danish philanthropic association focused on the built environment.
Henrik Mahncke, Realdania’s head of analysis, says high housing prices could partly explain the trend. Another possible reason is that many young people enjoy living with their parents.
However, where young people grow up also influences when they move out.
In Albertslund, a municipality near Copenhagen, 61 percent of 21-year-olds still live at home. On the island of Læsø, the figure is just 14 percent.
According to Statistics Denmark, distance to educational institutions is an important factor. Young people who live farther from places of study are more likely to move out.
Cultural background also plays a role, with young people from non-Western backgrounds generally staying at home longer.
Housing availability and prices may also influence their decisions.
Mette Mechlenborg, a senior researcher at Aalborg University who studies housing, points to another explanation: the design of modern family homes.
Many young people grow up in spacious houses with separate areas for parents and children, giving them greater privacy and independence.
This can make staying at home more attractive than moving into a small, expensive room.
Realdania’s study also found no overall difference in quality of life between young adults living with their parents and those who have moved out.
